candidates.name: UPGo-McGill/strr
candidates.what_it_holds: R package (422 commits, 5 stars) from McGill's Urban Politics and Governance lab (David Wachsmuth). Functions to clean/process raw AirDNA property and daily files, compress/expand STR tables, and CLASSIFY commercial operators, frequently-rented entire-home listings, 'ghost hostels', and units in actual housing stock -- i.e. a working multi-listing/professional-host detection methodology built for Canadian STR analysis. No data committed (works on external AirDNA input); license not stated in visible content.
candidates.why_useful: Directly relevant to gap #2 (realized ADR/occupancy) and the multi-listing/professional-host panel theme: an open, tested method for separating commercial hosts from casual hosts that our team could apply to any listing panel (including Inside Airbnb) rather than building from scratch.
candidates.last_activity: not dated precisely; 422 commits on master, active per issue count

candidates.name: UPGo-McGill organization (toronto-report-2023, bc-report-2024, bc-report-2023-summer, ontario-report-2024, vancouver-analysis, toronto-report, montreal-finance-2022)
candidates.what_it_holds: A multi-year series of Canadian city/province STR reports (Toronto, Vancouver, BC, Ontario) from an academic urban-policy lab that regularly publishes commercial-operator / multi-listing-host revenue-share statistics and STR registration-compliance analysis; repos have R/ and output/ folders (R code + rendered report, not raw CSV export as far as fetched). commercial-operators repo exists but its README says 'information temporarily removed for repo anonymization' (a student project, currently gutted).
candidates.why_useful: This is one of very few active research groups publishing recurring, city-level commercial/multi-listing host concentration numbers -- a proxy for professional-host share of STR supply outside the US, useful context for gap #12 (STR ordinance trackers/registration data) and the multi-listing host theme generally, even without a clean data file to pull.
candidates.size_hint: several small repos, R code + report PDFs

candidates.name: backmarket-oss/dac7
candidates.what_it_holds: Python tooling (138 commits) to build and validate DAC7 declarations for French tax authority (DGFiP): revised XSD schema, JSON schemas for platform-operator/entity-seller/individual-seller flat files, example files adapted from official DGFiP specs, CLI to build/validate/encrypt declarations. No actual DAC7 statistics or aggregate reported-income data -- only the filing schema/tooling. License: Etalab-2.0 (schemas/examples).
candidates.why_useful: Gives the exact data schema platforms like Airbnb must report to EU tax authorities under DAC7 (seller income, number of transactions, property addresses) -- useful for understanding what a DAC7 aggregate-statistics release would even look like if one is ever published, and for identifying the right EU government portals to check for aggregate DAC7 statistics.
candidates.size_hint: schema + example files, no bulk data

candidates.name: bcgov/House-Policy-STRDSS
candidates.what_it_holds: British Columbia government's 'Short Term Rental Data Sharing System' -- full-stack app (backend, frontend, PostgreSQL) that platforms operating in BC (Airbnb included) are required to report host/listing data into under BC's Short-Term Rental Accommodations Act. 2,764 commits, Apache-2.0 license. The repo itself is the government's internal software, not a public dataset or API; no public statistics endpoint found in the fetched README (only CI/CD/release docs).
candidates.why_useful: Confirms a real, government-mandated, DAC7-style platform-reporting regime exists for STR data in BC/Canada; worth a human checking gov.bc.ca or BC's open-data portal directly for any published aggregate statistics derived from this system (would be genuinely point-in-time regulatory data on host counts/compliance), even though the GitHub repo itself has no data.

candidates.name: rit-kalra/sql-toronto-str-analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: SQL-based analysis of Toronto's Airbnb market covering supply concentration, commercial host operations, licence compliance, and occupancy dynamics (student project, presumably built on Inside-Airbnb-style Toronto data).
candidates.why_useful: A small worked example of multi-listing/commercial-host classification queries on Toronto listings, a city not in our current 13-city Inside Airbnb panel.
candidates.size_hint: SQL scripts, unclear if data committed

notes: Session WebSearch quota was exhausted before this scout could run any WebSearch calls (shared budget across the sweep, 200/200 used by earlier scouts) -- worked entirely via WebFetch against github.com/search (worked well, occasionally 429'd -- back off and retry a different query), Zenodo's JSON API (zenodo.org/api/records?q=... -- works, the HTML zenodo.org/search page does not render via WebFetch), and Bing/DuckDuckGo (both effectively unusable via WebFetch -- Bing returns generic/irrelevant results, DuckDuckGo serves a CAPTCHA). HuggingFace's datasets search page also does not render useful content via WebFetch (client-rendered, shows filter chrome only). Overall finding: this theme (superhost/multi-listing host panels, host earnings, DAC7, IRS/tax STR income statistics) is genuinely thin on GitHub as *data* -- almost everything found is either (a) tooling to classify multi-listing/commercial hosts from AirDNA or Inside-Airbnb-shaped inputs (UPGo-McGill/strr is the strongest of these), (b) DAC7 tax-filing schema/tooling with zero actual reported statistics (backmarket-oss/dac7), (c) one real government platform-data-sharing system with no public output found (bcgov STRDSS), or (d) small single-city student projects applying a host-concentration lens to cities outside our panel (Toronto, Cape Town). No repo anywhere surfaces actual DAC7 aggregate statistics, IRS SOI short-term-rental income tables, or a genuine host-earnings panel with real dollar figures -- if such data exists publicly it is likely only on government statistical-office sites directly (Eurostat/national tax-authority DAC7 summary reports, IRS SOI bulletin tables), not mirrored on GitHub. Worth a follow-up scout checking Eurostat's DAC7-adjacent 'sharing economy' tables and the IRS SOI Tax Stats site directly (not GitHub) for a Schedule E / rental-income-by-AGI series, and a direct fetch of the Zenodo record files for the Santiago/Mexico City STR seasonality dataset flagged above to confirm what's actually in it.
